insSteps: Dissolve the yeast in half a glass of lukewarm water and a little sugar. Stir and let it foam for about 15 minutes.
Add the rest of the water, flour and salt, and mix. Knead the dough for about 5–7 minutes, until it becomes smooth, even, and elastic.
Lightly oil the mixing bowl, place the dough in it with a little oil on top, and cover.
Let it rise at room temperature until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
Gently press the dough down to release the air.
Turn it out onto the work surface. Divide into 6 pieces and flatten each into a round disc about 1 cm thick. Dust with flour and cover with a clean cloth.
Roll out each piece with a rolling pin to a thickness of about 5 mm
Heat a skillet over high heat. Grease the surface with a paper towel dipped in oil.
Place one piece of dough on the skillet and cook until small, timid bubbles begin to appear on the surface.
Flip the pita and continue cooking for a few more minutes, turning frequently. The pita should begin to puff up.
Remove each pita as it's done and wrap it in a clean kitchen towel.
Wipe the skillet with a paper towel. Continue until all the dough has been used.
Pitas are best eaten immediately after baking, while still warm. Otherwise, reheat them before serving.
